description: Conformance corpus for standards/060-auth.md. 'validity': the value must validate (or fail) against the named schema root — 'identity-token' or 'me'. 'behaviour': black-box cases a live deployment must satisfy. An implementation passes the whole file or names the case it fails.

validity.note: the irreducible token: who signed it, who it is for, when it dies, and the link key (AU2)
amr present so an application can require step-up without understanding how authentication happened (AU2)
THE case this shape exists for. A roles claim would make every application's access control depend on provider configuration, which is the failure the whole standard prevents (AU2)
without an audience a token minted for one application replays against another (AU2)
a subject is unique only within its issuer, so half the link key is not a key at all (AU3)
the application's own public id, never the provider's subject (IP1, AU6)
permissions are lowercase resource.action; casing drift is how two services stop agreeing about the same permission
an absent list and an empty list are different claims; requiring the field makes 'this user may do nothing here' explicit rather than inferred

behaviour.stimulus: present a well-formed identity token signed with a key the backend does not trust

expect.side_effect: no application state read or written

behaviour.note: the difference between verifying and decoding, which is the whole security value of variant (b) (AU2)

behaviour.stimulus: present a valid token whose aud names a different application
behaviour.note: without this check the portfolio's services are interchangeable to an attacker holding any one token (AU2)

behaviour.stimulus: authenticate successfully as an identity that has no local user record
behaviour.note: a 401 here loops forever: it returns an already-valid user to the provider, which authenticates them again (AU6)

behaviour.stimulus: revoke a user's access in application A, then authenticate as them at application B
behaviour.note: an application may remove its own grant and may never disable the identity (AU4)

behaviour.stimulus: invite the same email address from a second application
behaviour.note: ensureIdentity is idempotent and never claims ownership (AU4)

behaviour.stimulus: complete a login and inspect the Set-Cookie header

expect.name_prefix: __Host- in topology A, __Secure- in topology B

behaviour.note: HttpOnly is what puts the credential out of reach of injected script (AU7)

behaviour.stimulus: send OPTIONS to an API path with no cookie, from the client origin
behaviour.note: preflight is uncredentialed by specification; a proxy demanding a session on OPTIONS breaks every request before it starts (AU7)

behaviour.stimulus: in topology B, exceed a rate limit and read Retry-After from script
behaviour.note: without Access-Control-Expose-Headers the client cannot see it and HA7 silently stops applying (AU7)

behaviour.stimulus: fetch /me as a user whose identity link is known, and compare user.id against the provider's subject for that identity
behaviour.note: not schema-checkable, and the schema must not pretend otherwise: IP2 admits UUIDv7 as a public id format, so a bare UUID is legal and a subject that happens to be one is indistinguishable by shape. The property is real and the check has to compare two values, which only a live case can do (AU3, IP1)
